findings.reason: Independent inspection of all three original-resolution tiles and the full local example confirms six explicitly oriented affine face patches without an illustration. Opposite cube views with all six labels and a parameter-order legend materially clarify which patch has which outward area vector and why the same face is a graph face in one direction and lateral in the others. This is a warranted expository addition under the expanded diagram scope, rather than a defect in the existing proof.
findings.action: Appended two opposite cube views and six exact map/area-vector legend entries in the existing final Remarks section, with face-interior arrows and hidden edges.

diagram_math_checks.result: For z+,z-,x+,x-,y+,y-, the ordered derivative pairs are (e_x,e_y),(e_y,e_x),(e_y,e_z),(e_z,e_y),(e_z,e_x),(e_x,e_z). Their cross products are e_z,-e_z,e_x,-e_x,e_y,-e_y. Every arrow/legend label matches these signs. Positive vectors exit the face p_k=1 and negative vectors exit p_k=0.

diagram_math_checks.check: Two actual coordinate views and arrow placement
diagram_math_checks.result: The left drawing is the affine projection P(x,y,z)=(2x-2y,-0.7x-0.7y+2z); its visible faces are x+,y+,z+ and its labelled bottom vertex is P(1,1,0)=(0,-1.4). The right drawing uses P(1-x,1-y,1-z); its visible faces are x-,y-,z- and the same projected bottom vertex is now (0,0,1). In each drawing the three arrow displacements are (1.3,-0.455),(-1.3,-0.455),(0,1.3), equal to 0.65 times the corresponding projected outward basis vectors. Left arrow bases correspond to (1,0.5,0.525),(0.5,1,0.525),(0.5,0.5,1); right arrow bases are their coordinate complements, so every base lies in a face interior.

Closed faces meet only along their original boundary edges/vertices; arrows assert normals only in face interiors, so no smoothness or unique normal at corners is inferred.
